title: Six-month peak air temperature gave uncertain EPT richness slopes after mean control in four northern English samples in 1991-2017
abstract: We tested whether six-month peak air temperature had a negative link to river EPT family richness beyond six-month mean temperature. We used 5,562 autumn samples from northeast and northwest England in 1991-2003 and 2004-2017. Models controlled site, year and month, analysis method, sample day and curved mean temperature. Peak slopes were +0.128, -0.083, -0.564 and -0.190 families per C. All four corrected intervals included zero. Controls left only 0.22-0.35 C of peak variation. In early northwest England, the slope changed from -0.564 to +0.174 when we kept only flow-matched records, before flow adjustment. Flow adjustment then gave +0.149. This check shows why changed samples must be separated from added controls. These data do not establish a repeated peak-temperature deficit. Broad intervals do not show that heat has no effect. Air temperature is not stream temperature. Unknown field effort, coarse family counts, selected repeat sites and few year clusters limit inference. Regions have separate records but can share weather. Periods can share sites. We test no air-pollution effect. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and a figure are included; external record tables are excluded.

display.caption: Peak temperature slopes conditional on mean temperature and observation controls. Bars are Bonferroni intervals for four primary tests.

citations.reason: We adapt sample construction and checks. Biological records overlap. We test peak temperature conditional on mean temperature, rather than low flow by mean temperature.
Prior water-quality and warmth analysis from the same source archive. This is not independent data validation.
